newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singaporeans take high profile WTO meet in stride.
newsitem.headline: Singaporeans take high profile WTO meet in stride.

text.p: It has put Singapore on the world map but Singaporeans appear nonchalant about the ongoing World Trade Organisation (WTO) ministerial meeting.
"It is a good thing. It has put Singapore on the world map but I don't think anything is going to come out of this (meeting)," said Jean Sit, an assistant marketing manager, told Reuters.
"It is a bit "sikit atas" (over the top). I don't think Joe Blow in the street is interested in this," an oil trader at a European firm said.
Few, if any, are keeping tabs on the proceedings and many are of the opinion that the meeting is not likely to result in any major breakthrough in world trade
The WTO meeting started on Monday and has since been the scene of intense negotiations over various trade issues.
"It is a pretty event. Singapore is a logical choice (for the meeting), hopefully there is a pretty outcome," a research head at a local broking house said.
He said that some of the negotiations could "have negative corporate implications, especially on the telecommunications sector."

But others are hoping for cheaper phone bills once an agreement is made on freeing up basic telecommunications. Singapore officially on Wednesday informed the WTO of its decision to end Singapore Telecoms monopoly in March 31, 2000--seven years of the target date of 2007.

And while hoteliers in the Marina area where the convention is held are enjoying a boost in occupancy, retailers are complaining of slower sales as local shoppers shun the area due to the increased security.
The hassle of going around road blocks and security checkpoints has kept most shoppers to the more traditional Orchard Road shopping belt, retailers at the Suntec City mall told Reuters.
"Local shoppers are turned off by the high security," one retailer at the mall, who declined to be identified, said.
But most feel that in the longer term tourism in Singapore will benefit from the increased publicity of hosting such a high profile event.
WTO organisers said a total of 2,749 delegates from 128 member countries and 25 observer nations, and more importantly 1,652 journalists have registered to attend and cover the meeting.
Singapore's successful hosting of this mega event will also boost its image in the international convention circuit, Sit said.
"Singapore will surpass Hong Kong as Asia's main convention city soon," she said, but added that it would take another three years or more before this actually happens.
